## TL;DR

I reviewed the requested Hub, tailnet discovery, Releases, remote runner, and
check-plan documentation against the current implementation. The main finding
was that `user-docs/remote-engineers.md` still described the ADR 0009 proposal
as if remote engineer sessions were merely planned, and included configuration
that the product does not read. I replaced it with the shipped boundary:
managed engineer processes and task worktrees stay on the RepoOS host, while a
configured validation runner can perform the install/build/test portion of an
engineer's self-check. I added the requested QA record. No application code was
changed and no product bug requiring a follow-up was identified.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for a user-facing accuracy pass rather than a broad rewrite. I
started from the requested topic list and located the relevant pages under
`user-docs/`. Several pages are large reference manuals, so I used headings and
focused searches to inspect only the sections related to these behaviors.
For implementation evidence, I checked the current configuration schema and
defaults, the runner self-check path, runner CLI commands, tailnet discovery
configuration, and the Hub update UI.

The clearest discrepancy was `remote-engineers.md`. Its opening warning said
whole engineer sessions on runners were designed but not built, then it
presented a `[remoteEngineers]` block, runner placement options, host labels,
and board states as intended behavior. The current code instead exposes
`remoteValidation.engineerSelfCheckRemote`: when remote validation is enabled,
managed engineers can send install, build, and test work to a validation
runner. Format and lint remain local. The gate uses a verified checkout and a
green pass can be reused at handoff for the same commit. The engineer CLI,
task worktree, and engineer subprocess itself continue to run on the machine
hosting RepoOS. I removed the hypothetical configuration and replaced the page
with the actual behavior, setup pointers, and a compact table showing where
each part runs.

I also made the toggle behavior explicit. `engineerSelfCheckRemote` defaults
to enabled when remote validation itself is enabled. Setting it to false
returns the full self-check to the RepoOS host. This distinction prevents the
misreading that turning off the remote portion only moves a subset of the
gate, or that the setting enables remote engineer execution.

The macOS Hub page already describes the current manual stable-release check,
the six-hour result cache and explicit recheck, and the browser-based download
flow rather than an in-app updater. Its local server menu and current window
layouts were consistent with the application. The Android page accurately
describes APK updates and signing, querying tailnet peers through a saved
server, filtering peers, and requiring HTTPS for selected remote server URLs.
The phone does not scan the network itself. Configuration docs accurately
state that `tailnetDiscovery` is on by default and applied independently to
each project, even when several RepoOS servers share a host.

The check documentation accurately describes project-owned `[[check.steps]]`
plans, changed-path behavior, and the remote engineer self-check. The Releases
page documentation I inspected was consistent with current release checks,
prerelease handling, release-note drafting and publish safeguards, and
distribution destinations. I did not expand the review into unrelated portions
of the configuration reference or claim live device coverage.

The requested QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-user-docs-accuracy.md`. It lists
the concrete change and summarizes the reviewed topics with no-change findings.
It also states that no implementation bug was found and that this QA pass did
not run device-specific testing.

## Approaches tried

I first searched the specified user-docs pages by subject terms and headings.
This surfaced the stale remote-runner page quickly and showed that the relevant
Hub topics are distributed across dedicated pages and the large configuration
reference. I then inspected narrow excerpts instead of reading whole reference
files. Finally, I used implementation searches to verify the documentation's
claims against the current source: the self-check setting and runner gate, the
Hub update component and release status route, and `tailnetDiscovery` config
parsing and registry behavior.

I considered leaving the remote engineer page as an ADR-era forward-looking
guide with a warning, but that would preserve incorrect options and operational
steps that users could mistake for usable configuration. Replacing it with the
currently supported feature is more useful and avoids promising future
capabilities. I retained the page title because it remains a useful landing
place for users searching for remote engineer execution, while making the
first paragraph directly answer that the managed engineer process itself is
not remote today.

## Challenges and blockers

The terminology is easy to confuse: “remote runners” now cover validation
checks and browser evidence, but that does not mean the engineer process moved
off-host. The source names the supported self-check feature through
`remoteValidation.engineerSelfCheckRemote`, and its implementation splits
local format/lint from remotely dispatched install/build/tests. I wrote the
page to keep those boundaries explicit and to avoid reusing the obsolete
`remoteEngineers` placement vocabulary.

The code review was read-only beyond the documentation task. I did not change
`repoos.toml`, source, test files, or task metadata. No blockers were found.
The worktree remains on its assigned task branch; RepoOS owns the check result,
commit, and handoff lifecycle.

## Key learnings

The durable documentation lesson is to distinguish the location of the agent
process from the location of its validation gate. A project may use a remote
runner for selected or managed self-check work without running the agent CLI or
its worktree remotely. Docs should name the exact setting that controls this
and describe its default only in the context where it applies (remote
validation enabled).

For this pass, documentation inspection was strongest when each user-facing
statement was paired with its owner in code: config parsing/defaults for
settings, server gate orchestration for where checks run, and UI behavior for
what the Hub shows. The QA record makes the reviewed scope and the limits of
verification visible, so later reviewers can distinguish a source-backed
behavior check from unperformed device QA.
